newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Jiang says no interference in North Korea.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang says no interference in North Korea.

text.p: China's President Jiang Zemin said on Friday that Beijing would not interfere in the affairs of its communist neighbour North Korea but would work to promote stability on the divided Korean peninsula.
North Korea has been hit by years of natural disaster that have accelerated its economic decline and produced near famine conditions, international aid workers say.
China would help Pyongyang through its grain shortage as far as was possible, Jiang told U.S. broadcaster Cable News Network (CNN) in an interview.
Asked if China had offered Pyongyang advice on how to survive the crisis and preserve peace with its arch-rival South Korea, Jiang said Beijing would not interfere.

"With regard to the question of how the DPRK (Democratic People's Republic of Korea) should be run, it is our consistent principle that we do not interfere in the internal affairs of other countries," he said, declining to comment further.
North and South Korea are still technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce. Chinese troops backed the North Koreans during the war.
But trade between China and South Korea have mushroomed in recent years, and ties have thawed.
